source_observations_reviewed.observation: Logical rules require acted-on sentences at a far end, so Exchange moves adjacent A/B positions; Contraction combines two identical copies; Weakening adds an arbitrary sentence on either side.
source_observations_reviewed.handling: Keep the operational roles and both-sided displays distinct. Do not describe Exchange as moving between sequent sides, Contraction as deletion of an arbitrary sentence, or Weakening as replacement.

source_observations_reviewed.observation: Double inference lines abbreviate a series of weakening, contraction and exchange inferences. Cut is said not to be strictly necessary but useful for reusing and combining derivations, and eliminates the shared formula A between two premises.
source_observations_reviewed.handling: Retain the abbreviation scope, non-necessity qualification, reuse/combine rationale, binary premise contexts and exact lower concatenation order.

source_observations_reviewed.observation: A derivation is either an initial sequent alone or one/two derivations followed by an inference; equivalently it is a finite sequent tree with initial sequents at the top, designated S at the bottom and every other node serving as a premise of a correct rule application immediately below it.
source_observations_reviewed.handling: Keep both formulations, finiteness, all three enumerated conditions, one-or-two premise arity, tree orientation, end-sequent and derivable terminology exact.

source_observations_reviewed.observation: The generic weakening rule is instantiated from C sequent C with A played by D and both Gamma/Delta played by C; the exchange instance then has Gamma/Pi empty, Delta=C, A=D and B=C. The generic exchange display contains a literal comma inside its concluding math expression.
source_observations_reviewed.handling: Preserve each role assignment, empty context, sentence order and every displayed tree. Retain the source comma rather than silently editing formal punctuation in this translation batch.

source_observations_reviewed.observation: The first combination matches Gamma to C,D, empty Delta, A=C and B=D, yielding C,D sequent C-and-D. Reversing the binary premises swaps A/B roles and yields D-and-C, while the antecedent stays C,D.
source_observations_reviewed.handling: Keep the last sequents as the rule premises, preserve every empty-context statement, and do not use commutativity to normalize the two visibly different conjunction conclusions.
